messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details:
The test `testTwoCompleteOptions()` creates Options using the `OptionBuilder`. The first Option is created with a type explicitly set to `Float.class` via `withType(Float.class)`. The second Option is created without explicitly setting a type, so the type is not set.

The bug report states that `getParsedOptionValue` returns null unless the Option's type is explicitly set. The user expects the type to be `String` by default unless it is set to any other type.

Inspecting the `OptionBuilder.create(String)` method shows that it creates a new Option and then calls `option.setType(type);` where `type` is a field set by the builder. If no type was set by the builder, this passed `type` will be `null`.

The `Option` class keeps the type in a field and returns it via `getType()`. This would be `null` unless explicitly set.

`CommandLine.getParsedOptionValue(String)` calls `option.getType()` and passes it to `TypeHandler.createValue(String, Class)`. 

`TypeHandler.createValue(String, Class)` returns different parsed values depending on the Class passed in. Importantly, if the class is `null`, it ends up returning `null`. The null type thus results in `getParsedOptionValue` returning null rather than returning the original String value.

From this analysis, the root cause of the failure is that when no type is explicitly set for an Option, its type is `null` instead of defaulting to `String.class`. This leads to `getParsedOptionValue` returning null.

The solution could be implemented either:
- at the Option creation to default the Option's type to String if no explicit type is set;
- or within `CommandLine.getParsedOptionValue` to treat a null Option type as String for parsing.

In addition, documenting this behavior clearly in the Javadocs would help clarify expectations.

Hence, the bug occurs because the Option type field defaults to null rather than String, leading to null returns in getParsedOptionValue for Options without explicitly set types, as demonstrated in the failing test.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
